content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted. **This is the first SDD gate — please review it before we plan or build anything.**

- **Spec:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`
- **Quality checklist:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md` (all items pass; no open clarifications)

## What the spec proposes — a quick tour

**The core idea:** a single-user, browser-based app to save links and find them again later. No accounts/login in v1.

**User journeys, in priority order:**
1. **Save a bookmark** (P1) — paste a URL, optional title/tags, it persists. *This alone is a usable product.*
2. **Browse & search** (P2) — list newest-first, keyword search over title and address.
3. **Edit & delete** (P2) — correct or remove bookmarks, with a delete confirmation.
4. **Organize with tags** (P3) — tag bookmarks and filter by a tag.

**Notable decisions I made (please confirm or push back):**
- **No auto-fetching** of page titles/favicons/previews in v1 — titles are typed or derived from the URL.
- **No import/export or browser extension** in v1 — manual entry only.
- **Duplicate URLs** trigger a warning rather than silently saving twice.
- **URLs without `http://`** are accepted and normalized.
- Success targets like *save first bookmark in under 30s* and *search 500 bookmarks in under 1s*.

## A few things worth your steer

1. **Single-user with no login** — is that right, or do you expect accounts / multiple users?
2. **v1 scope exclusions** — are you OK leaving out auto-fetched titles/favicons and import/export for now?
3. **Tags** as the organizing model (vs. folders, or nothing at all)?

Per our spec-driven workflow, I'm **pausing here and not moving to planning yet**. Tell me if the spec looks right or what you'd like changed — once you approve, I'll run **speckit-plan** for the implementation plan (the next gate).

Single-user with no login is right, and tags are the organization I want rather than folders.

I’m not ready to approve the specification yet, though. A few important behaviours need changing or filling in:

- Saving a link should automatically collect its title, description, favicon, and preview image. I should still be able to edit the title and description.
- If I save an address that already exists, don’t merely warn me; take me to the existing bookmark so I can update it.
- Search should ignore letter case and cover the title, address, description, notes, and tags. I also want exact phrases, `#tag` searches, and combinations such as AND, OR, NOT, and parentheses.
- When entering tags, suggest tags I have already used.
- I need a “read later” state with a separate unread view, plus a way to mark items read.
- I need archiving as a reversible alternative to deletion, with archived links hidden from the normal list and available in their own view.
- I expect to select several bookmarks—or everything matching my current search or filter—and apply actions such as adding/removing tags, marking read/unread, archiving, or deleting.
- I need sorting choices, not only newest first.
- Each bookmark should support a description and a formatted note.
- I want a preserved copy of the linked page, including keeping a PDF when the link points to one, and an option to save it through the Internet Archive.
- I want reusable saved views made from a search and included or excluded tags.
- Please include bookmark import and export in the common browser-bookmark HTML format; importing should retain titles, tags, and dates.
- Basic display preferences such as default sorting, how many items are shown, and text size should be included.

A browser extension can remain out of scope. Please revise the specification around these points and bring it back for approval before planning.

Both details are in, and your three defaults are now recorded as confirmed decisions. **Revised spec is back at the gate** — `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`.

## What I added this round

**Search operator vs. quoted words** (US-3 scenarios 6–7, new **FR-012a** / **FR-012b**):
- `and` / `or` / `not` act as **boolean operators only when unquoted**; inside quotes (e.g. `"rock and roll"`) they're matched as **ordinary words**.
- A query can **mix `#tag` terms with ordinary text** and evaluate them together under the same boolean logic and grouping — e.g. `#work AND report` → bookmarks tagged `work` whose content matches `report`.

**Main-list display** (US-3 scenarios 1 & 1a, new **FR-028** / **FR-029**):
- Every row **clearly shows title, description, tags, and favicon**.
- **Selecting/activating a row opens the original link** in a new tab — kept explicitly distinct from the checkbox-style multi-select used for bulk actions, so the two don't conflict.

**Confirmed decisions** section now records your three answers: markdown-style notes, single snapshot at save time, and Internet Archive best-effort (failures never touch the bookmark or its local copy).

Post-design constitution re-check: still **PASS** (no violations introduced). No `after_plan` hooks (no extensions.yml). The planning gate artifacts are complete.

## Implementation plan is ready for your review — planning gate

**Branch/feature**: `001-bookmark-manager` · **Plan**: `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md`

Generated artifacts:
- `plan.md` — technical approach, structure, gates
- `research.md` — 11 key technical decisions (each with rationale + alternatives)
- `data-model.md` — entities, SQLite schema, FTS index, states
- `contracts/api.md` — HTTP/JSON API
- `contracts/search-grammar.md` — the advanced-search language + how it compiles
- `quickstart.md` — how to run + validation steps mapped to your acceptance criteria

## The approach in plain terms

- **One web app**: a small Node/TypeScript server (Fastify) that serves a React single-page front end and a JSON API, listening where the review environment expects it (port 4000).
- **Storage**: a local SQLite database file for bookmarks/tags/views/preferences, plus a folder on disk for the **preserved page copies** and retained **PDFs**. Everything survives restarts; nothing external to install.
- **Automatic capture** (title/description/favicon/preview + the page snapshot) runs **in the background right after you save**, so saving stays instant even if a site is slow or down. Each bookmark shows a capture status so you can see when metadata isn't available.
- **Search** is built as a proper little query language: it parses your query (phrases, `#tag`, AND/OR/NOT, parentheses, and the "operators-only-when-unquoted" rule) and translates it into fast database queries that combine tag and text conditions correctly.
- **Page preservation** captures a single self-contained snapshot at save time (keeps the PDF as-is when the link is a PDF), with an optional, best-effort Internet Archive submission that never affects your local copy if it fails.
- **Import/export** uses the standard browser bookmark HTML format, preserving titles/tags/dates and merging (not duplicating) links you already have.
- **Testing** focuses unit tests on the riskiest logic (search parser, URL normalization, import/export) plus a few end-to-end checks of the main journey.

## Worth flagging

- **Persistence choice**: I chose **SQLite (a local file)** rather than a separate database server — simplest and durable for a single-user app. Happy to revisit if you'd prefer something else.
- **Preserved copies grow disk usage** over time (they're full page captures). Stored as files to keep things manageable; retention tuning was deferred in the spec — we can add a cap later if you want.
- This remains a **sizable build** (13 user stories). The plan is structured so P1 (save + list/search) is a working slice first, then P2/P3 layer on.

Per the workflow I'm **pausing before any code**. If the plan looks right, **approve it** and I'll proceed to **speckit-tasks** (the actionable task breakdown) — and then, once you're happy, **speckit-implement**.

The gap is closed and made explicit in both artifacts. **Plan is back at the planning gate for approval.**

## What I changed

**Spec** (source of truth):
- **FR-019** now states that "matching the current view" must honor the **complete active criteria** — including a saved view's query *and* its included/excluded tags — across the **entire** result set, not just the visible page or the text/simple-tag portion.
- **US-9 scenario 2a** added, spelling out the saved-view case explicitly.

**Plan / API contract** (how it's guaranteed):
- The bulk endpoint's `match` selector now accepts the **exact same criteria as the list endpoint** (`q`, `tag[]`, `view`, `scope`).
- Introduced **one shared query builder** (`search/resolveView.ts`) used by **both** listing and bulk selection. When a saved view is active, it applies the view's stored query and its include/exclude tags in full, computed server-side over the whole set (pagination ignored).
- Because both paths run through the same builder, a bulk action affects **exactly** what the current view shows — structurally, they can't drift apart.

## HTML preservation corrected — self-contained snapshots

This was a fidelity bug against the approved spec (FR-022 / plan research §5), so I fixed the implementation against the spec — no spec/plan/tasks changes needed.

**What changed:** a new inliner (`backend/src/services/inline.ts`) now runs during capture and makes each HTML snapshot fully self-contained:
- **Stylesheets** are fetched and embedded as inline `<style>` — including their `url(...)` assets (background images, fonts) and `@import`ed CSS, resolved and embedded recursively.
- **Images** are embedded as `data:` URIs; `srcset`/`<picture><source>` (which would re-fetch remote variants) are removed.
- **Favicons/icons** are embedded too.
- **Scripts and live-linked resources** (preload/prefetch) are stripped so nothing reaches the network at view time.
- It's bounded and best-effort (per-asset timeout, 4 MB/asset, ~24 MB/snapshot budget); an unfetchable asset is dropped rather than failing the snapshot.
- **PDF preservation is unchanged** — the original file is retained verbatim, as you asked.

**Verified with the original resources unavailable — two ways:**
1. **Automated test** (`backend/tests/integration/snapshot.test.ts`): serves a page with external CSS, a CSS `url()` background, an image, and a script; captures it; **shuts the origin server down**; then asserts the served snapshot contains the inlined CSS rule and `data:` image URIs, contains **no** live asset references, and has no `<script>`.
2. **Live run against the actual server**: captured a local site, **killed the origin (HTTP 000)**, then fetched `/api/bookmarks/:id/snapshot` — result: inlined `<style>` ✓, CSS rule present ✓, data-URI images ✓, no `site.css`/`pic.png`/`bg.png` live refs ✓, scripts stripped ✓.

**Also found and fixed a process issue:** your earlier session had a detached server still running the pre-fix code (my new start hit `EADDRINUSE`). I stopped it; the port is now free so the next launch runs the corrected code.

**Full status:** 34/34 tests pass (added the snapshot test), typecheck and ESLint clean, frontend built, `.harness/app.json` in place.
